messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: coord_flip() breaks geom_hline()
parts:
#dummy data
a=as.data.frame(cbind(v1=1:10,v2=11:20))

#set up the basic plot
p = ggplot(data=a,aes(x=v1,y=v2))+geom_point()

p+geom_hline(yintercept=15) #looks ok!

p+geom_hline(yintercept=15)+coord_flip() #where'd the line go?

#try some fixes
p+coord_flip()+geom_hline(yintercept=15) #still missing
p+coord_flip()+geom_vline(xintercept=15) #odd placement & doesn't fill the plot
p+geom_vline(xintercept=15)+coord_flip() #again, odd placement & doesn't fill the plot

#Help?

messages.author: 98596efc7c661bfd
messages.subject: Re: coord_flip() breaks geom_hline()
parts:
Not quite the same example, but I just ran into this interaction
between coord_flip() and geom_hline() yesterday, while using
geom_crossbar() + coord_flip() to put some ordered categorical data
(variable point estimates + error ranges, from an OLS model) on the y-
axis. I wanted to show a vertical line at zero on the (displayed) x-
axis. I found that geom_segment() worked where geom_hline() did not,
though obviously the line's beginning and endpoints had to be
explicitly specified, with the value of the end point set equal to the
number of categories.

Kieran

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: coord_flip() breaks geom_hline()
parts:
For all that they seem so simple, geom_vline and geom_hline are two of
the hardest geoms to get working correctly, and I still haven't worked
out all the glitches with some combinations of coordinate systems. As
Kieran says, you might want to use geom_segment directly, which should
give you fewer problems.

Regards,

Hadley
